notes.basket: The breakfast basket, an average index of coffee, sugar, wheat, and orange juice prices benchmarked to 2015 (set at 100), currently stands at 132, reflecting a 32% increase since 2015. This indicates that on average, these key soft commodity prices have risen notably over this period. The rise has been uneven across components and has occurred primarily in recent years. These figures are drawn from global commodity prices tracked by FRED and the IMF.
notes.movers: The most significant price changes since 2015 are coffee up 93% and orange juice up 22%, with wheat and sugar seeing relatively modest increases of 7% and 5%, respectively. These price movements largely reflect weather-related and disease impacts in thin, specialized markets—such as frost and drought in coffee-growing regions, and citrus greening and hurricanes affecting orange juice production—rather than broad-based inflationary pressures. The sensitivity of these crops to environmental factors results in pronounced volatility in their markets.
notes.why: The headline basket increase is driven by a few key weather-exposed soft commodities, underscoring the impact of environmental risks on global food prices. Given the nature of these crops and their susceptibility to climate events and diseases, elevated price levels may persist for extended periods. Stakeholders should consider that these supply-side shocks can maintain upward pressure on prices beyond short-term market cycles.
